answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a scarce reputation bond earned only through verified useful work, like a garden that only grows jade after real seasons of tending, never from planting a thousand empty plots overnight. Each new identity starts at zero trust and must echo the checked work of established peers before its outputs are attested and credited. An attacker spinning up fake agents pays the full cost of real work per identity, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand times the effort, while honest agents keep compounding trust.
